subject.title: Bug: Billing error (402) causes infinite retry death spiral for inline-apiKey providers (no backoff)

question: Should OpenClaw make inline `models.providers.<id>.apiKey` credentials participate in persisted provider-level auth/billing cooldowns and fail closed during active cooldown windows?
rationale: The source-level bug is clear, but the fix creates a durable provider-scoped cooldown identity and changes upgrade behavior for existing inline-key users, so maintainer product and compatibility intent is required before landing.

options.title: Accept provider-level cooldown
options.body: Land or rebuild the linked fix so inline keys get the same billing/auth cooldown protection as profile-backed credentials while preserving healthy stored-profile fallback.

options.title: Keep profile-only cooldowns
options.body: Document auth profiles as the supported billing-backoff path and leave inline API keys as immediate-retry credentials.

options.title: Request narrower design
options.body: Pause the linked PR until maintainers specify the exact cooldown identity, persistence, fallback, and recovery behavior they want.

recommendation.title: Accept provider-level cooldown
recommendation.body: Land or rebuild the linked fix so inline keys get the same billing/auth cooldown protection as profile-backed credentials while preserving healthy stored-profile fallback.

likelyOwner.reason: Peter has the strongest current-main history across model auth, provider runtime auth seams, and adjacent auth/failover policy in the implicated files.
